claims: E15 is a gasoline blend containing 15% ethanol and 85% gasoline.
E15 is approved for use in 2001 and newer light-duty vehicles.
E15 is often sold as Unleaded 88.
E15 offers higher octane compared to standard 10% ethanol (E10) fuel.
E15 offers lower emissions compared to E10.
E15 has generally lower prices (about 10 cents less per gallon) compared to E10.
As of May 2026, the EPA is allowing nationwide, year-round sales of E15 to reduce pump prices.
E15 is available at over 3,000 stations.
E15 is available primarily in the Midwest.
E15 is safe for most 2001 and newer cars, light-duty trucks, and SUVs.
E15 is safe for flex-fuel vehicles (FFVs).
E15 can damage engines and fuel systems of motorcycles, boats, chainsaws, lawnmowers, or older vehicles.
Ethanol has a lower energy density compared to pure gasoline.
Ethanol's lower energy density may cause a slight decrease in fuel efficiency (miles per gallon) compared to pure gasoline.
E15's higher octane can improve performance.
E15 reduces greenhouse gas emissions by roughly 3% compared to E10.
